=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:517 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The error message extraction logic does not decode percent-encoding.
  WHY: gh_retry wraps the error in `::warning::  stderr: ...` and percent-encodes `%`, newlines (`%0A`) and carriage returns (`%0D`); the awk strips the prefix but leaves the encoded characters, so the CI warning is unreadable for complex errors. Hardening fix: `if (sub(/^::warning::[ \t]*stderr: /, "", l)) { gsub(/%0[AD]/, "\n", l); gsub(/%25/, "%", l) }` (HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1).
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

  WHY: A DELETE failure whose stderr contains `%` or a multi-line JSON body is logged with literal `%0A`/`%25`. The step still exits 0 and the structured line is unaffected. The `FAKE_GH_STALE_FUNC` `delete_mode="fail"` stub is single-line with no `%`, so it cannot catch this.
- scripts/review_autofix_step_post_editor_summary.sh:518 | severity=NIT | confidence=4

  WHY: Operators see percent-encoded text whenever the error spans more than one line or contains `%`. That conflicts with the repo tests (`tests/test_gh_retry_final_stderr_redaction.py:54`, `tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py:27884,27913,27938`, `tests/test_review_autofix_review_pipeline_contract.py:10093`), which treat these as live tokens.
